findings.reason: the node that builds the cut must either subtract ruled exceptions (the ruling sentence, contradicting "uncorrected, over every member") or not (the refusal clause, which then makes §4's exception route for sourceless members dead), and with equilibrium at 210 members carrying any single unrepairable defect the whole first-group cut lands on the wrong side of that choice.
findings.text: the section rules that a group is cut when every member is judged sound "or is a named exception the lead has ruled" and that an undecidable member counts as defective "until it is ruled", but the done-when in the same section defines the rate as "the share of members the blind adjudication of §4 judges defective, taken over every member and uncorrected, with the members it cannot decide reported as their own share", and refuses the cut when that rate "is above the ruled bar", now 0; nothing subtracts a ruled exception from the rate, so any group holding one defective or undecidable member — including the sourceless member §4 clears by "listing with the lead's ruling as an exception the bar reads" — is refused by the measured clause while the ruling clause admits it, and the node cannot tell which of the two decides
